Commentary.Commentary: So Bangladesh need 212 to book their place in the final against their Asian counterparts. New Zealand have the momentum and will be happy with the score they have got on board. Can the Black Caps defend it or will the Bangla Tigers roar into the finals? Join us in a while to find out.

The star of New Zealand's batting, Beckham Wheeler-Greenall is caught down for a quick chat. Beckham says it was a tough start as the spinners were bowling well. Tells his mind-set was to dominate from the start and take on the spinners. Tells it was tough to play strokes on this pitch but got a bit easier as he started to time the ball.

It was a very good bowling performance from the Bangla Tigers but they will be disappointed with their overall effort in the end. They were on top and would have looked to restrict them under 160 but the Asian side lost its plot towards the end. Shoriful Islam was very good in the start but his final over spoiled his day a bit as he went away for 19. He though was the pick of the bowlers and finished with 3 wickets. Murad was good and economical as he finished with 2/34 from his 10. Shamim Hossain and Rakibul Hasan were the other bowlers to get into the wickets column with 2 and 1 each.

After being put into bat, New Zealand struggled to score runs as they kept losing wickets at regular intervals. With the scorecard reading 74/4 it looked like the Kiwis would struggle to get to 150 but underestimate the Black Caps at your own risk. Lidstone and Wheeler-Greenall then steadied the ship and built a crucial partnership of 67. Lidstone departed soon into the final Powerplay but Wheeler-Greenall did not lose his focus and took the charge in the final 10 overs, getting his fifty in the process. His unbeaten 75 off just 83 balls ensured that New Zealand enter the break with a very good total.

What a finish from New Zealand! They have managed to score 72 runs in the last 10 overs and have got well past the 200-run mark. They end the innings with the momentum and a competitive total on the board. Bangladesh will be a tad disappointed and would feel they have given away 20-30 runs more.

New Zealand steal a bye off the last ball. Full and well wide outside off, Wheeler-Greenall moves towards the off side and looks to paddle but then seeing it is wide of the tramline he looks to guide it towards third man. He misses and they take a run. The umpire signals it as bye. New Zealand FINISH WITH 211/8!
WIDE! Too wide outside off from Islam. Wheeler-Greenall moves across but lets it go and the umpire has wided that.

Pressure gets the better of Shoriful. Good length ball outside off, Ashok looks to paddle it but misses. Beckham calls for a quick run. The keeper sends an underarm throw to the bowler. Ashok is well short but Shoriful fails to score a direct hit at the bowler's end. He should have hit the stumps there.
FOUR! In the gap and a very good shot from Ashok. Full on middle and off, Adithya whips it in the gap between long on and deep mid-wicket for a boundary.

OUT! Caught! Field holes out. Brilliant comeback from Shoriful. He has the last laugh. After going for 10 off the first two, Shoriful bangs it a bit short. Field looks to cut it over point. He does not time it well and ends up hitting it to the man at deep point. Hasan Murad there comes running in and takes a very good catch. Can't blame Field for going after it as this is the time where batters throw everything at it. Wheeler-Greenall will be on strike as the batsmen crossed ends there.

He is taking his side closer to the 200-mark here. Wheeler-Greenall raises his bat and appreciates the applause he is getting from his teammates and fans here.

Murad gets his second of the game and he has his arms up in celebration.

OUT! LBW! The well-set Lindstone is out of here and Bangladesh have got rid of this stand as well. The last thing New Zealand would have wanted was to see the back of either of the two batsmen at the start of Powerplay 3 but that is what has happened here. Shoriful bowls a low full toss on middle and leg, Lidstone tries to flick it on the leg side but he misses. The ball hits him flush on the pads. He will be furious to get out on a full toss after having his eye in. Bangladesh players go up in a confident appeal and the umpire slowly raises his finger. The 67-run stand is broken and Shoriful finally has a wicket to his name. He has been excellent today and has the wicket his performance deserves.

NOT OUT! The third umpire agrees with the on-field umpire and signals it as Not Out on the giantscreen. Good length ball on middle, Wheeler-Greenall comes down the track and yorks himself. He manages to dig it to the side of the pitch on the off side. Lindstone calls for a quick run, Shoriful charges towards the ball. Nicholas grounds his bat but takes the ball with him. He raises his hands up to apologies. The Bangladesh players though put in an appeal for obstructing the field. The umpires have a brief chat and take it to the T.V. umpire with the soft signal as Not Out. Replay rolls in and it shows Lindstone neither changed  his run up nor was it intentional to get his bat on ball.

The Bangladesh players are going up in appeal for obstructing the field. They feel Lindstone came in the way intentionally. The on-field umpires have taken it upstairs with the soft signal as NOT OUT!

OUT! Bowled! The Kiwi skipper is out of here. Once again it is the spinner who gets the wicket. The scoreboard pressure gets the better of Jesse Tashkoff. Tossed up delivery pitching on middle. Tashkoff makes a bit of room and looks to drive it on the off side. He leaves a big gap between the bat and pad. The ball skids off the surface and turns in just a bit. It goes right between the gate of bat and pad and goes on to hit the middle and leg poles. The leg pole is uprooted and once again New Zealand lose a wicket when it looked like they were getting some momentum. New Zealand in troubled waters as they are not just struggling to score runs but are losing wickets as well.

How has Lidstone survived that? Flighted delivery on middle and leg, it turns away from there. Lidstone looks to sweep but misses. The ball kisses his arm and then the back leg and luckily for him it misses the stumps later on. There is a stifled appeal for LBW but it has been turned down by the umpire.

The replays later roll in and it confirms that the umpire was right.

OUT! CAUGHT! Brilliant catch from Mahmudul Hasan Joy. Fantastic effort in the field. Lovely sight to see the commitment from the fielder. Hossain goes shorter and flatter outside off. Lellman fetches the ball from there and goes for the pull. He hits hard but uppishly to the right of the man at short mid-wicket. It goes quickly on that side of Mahmudul Hasan Joy. Hasan Joy dives to his right and plucks it out of thin air. A budding partnership is cut short and Bangladesh continue to pick wickets at regular intervals. Bangladesh have been very energetic in the field today and this wicket belongs to Mahmudul Hasan Joy as much as it belongs to Shamim Hossain.

Flighted delivery on middle, Lidstone looks to defend but gets an inside edge onto the pads. The bowler appeals for lbw but the umpire shakes his head.
BEATEN! Tossed up delivery outside off, Lidstone looks to drive but misses it.
Floated delivery on middle, Lellman flicks it through mid-wicket for a single.
Full delivery on off, Lidstone drives it through covers for a single.
Flighted delivery outside off, Lidstone offers no shot to this one.
Tossed up delivery on off, Lidstone defends it off the front foot.
BEATEN! Good length delivery just outside off, Lellman looks to defend but misses it.
On a good length on middle, Lellman keeps it out.
Full delivery on middle, Lellman drives it back towards the bowler.
On a good length on middle, Lellman blocks it off the back foot.
Good length delivery on off, Lellman defends it out.
On a good length and outside off, Lellman offers no shot to this one.
Full delivery on middle, Lidstone drives it towards mid on. Wicket maiden over from Rakibul Hasan.
Tossed up delivery on middle, Lidstone defends it off the back foot.
Nicholas Lidstone is out to bat.

OUT! Caught behind! Bangladesh players are up in joy once again as Ollie White departs. Another wicket off the spinner and New Zealand are off to a very bad start. Just when White and this partnership was settling in Rakibul comes and sends Ollie back to the pavilion. Floated delivery outside off, it is bowled slightly slower through the air. Ollie loses his concentration and goes for the drive. The ball turns in off the surface and kisses the outside edge of White's bat. Skipper, Akbar Ali behind the stumps takes it and goes up in appeal and the umpire raises his finger. Rakibul has his dancing shoes on as he celebrates.
Loopy delivery on off, White keeps it out.
Flighted delivery on middle, White looks to flick but gets hit on the thigh pad. The bowler appeals for lbw but the umpire shakes his head.
Tossed up delivery on off, White defends it off the front foot.
Length delivery on off, White punches it through point for a single.
Outside off, White shoulders arms to this one.
BEATEN AGAIN! Good length delivery outside off, White comes down the track and looks to drive but misses it.
BEATEN! On a good length and outside off, White looks to defend but misses it.

FOUR! Nicely played! White breaks the shackles with this shot. White comes down the track and makes some room by going away from the stumps. He connects well with the ball and lofts it over mid off and fetches himself a boundary.
Tossed up delivery on middle, White looks to defend but gets hit on the thigh pad.
Powerplay 2 is signalled. Maximum of 4 fielders will be outside the 30-yard circle till the 40th over.
Flatter and around off, Lellman blocks it off the back foot to the side off the pitch. End of Powerplay 1. New Zealand are 26/1 after 10 overs.
Floated ball on off, Lellman shows the full face of the bat and blocks it off the back foot.
Floated ball outside off, Lellman lets the ball go.
Floated ball on off, Lellman blocks it off the front foot.
Tossed up ball outside off, Lellman lets it be.
Tossed up on off, driven to covers.
Driven through mid-off by the batsman.

FOUR! White is lucky to not edge that behind. Sakib just bowls on a length and gets it away from the left-hander. White throws his bat at it and gets it off the outside edge past the second slip for a boundary at third man.
Length ball on off, White pushes the ball to mid off.
Length ball on middle, White flick it to mid-wicket.
Full ball outside off, White looks to lay bat on ball but the ball sneaks through him past the outside edge.
Length ball outside off, defended off the back foot to covers.
Tanzim Hasan Sakib is on now.
Tossed up delivery on middle, Lellman flicks it to mid-wicket.
Flighted delivery on middle, Lellman pushes it back towards the bowler.
Flighted delivery on middle, Lellman keeps it out.
Full delivery on off, Lellman drives it to covers.
Tossed up delivery on off, Lellman defends it off the front foot.
Full toss on off, Lellman drives it back towards the bowler.
Rakibul Hasan is into the attack.
Full and on off, White blocks it off the back foot.

NOT OUT! White survives there. Islam in search of a wide yorker dishes out a low full toss. White gets his bat on the ball and the ball goes straight to the fielder at point. The fielder appeals for a catch and the umpire take it upstairs to check it. The Soft signal is Not Out and the replays roll in it shows that the ball bounced on the turf after hitting the bat. Ollie White stays to fight another day. Can he capitalise on this?
Is that a bump ball? The umpires have got together and taken it upstairs. The soft signal is NOT OUT!

FOUR! Very nicely played by Ollie White. Full and angled on the pads, White leans and flicks it through mid-wicket. The fielder from fine leg runs across to his right but the ball beats him to meet the fence there.
Bouncer! Short ball on off, White ducks under it.
Length ball on off, White blocks it off the back foot towards covers.
White is down in pain and the physio is out to have a quick check on him.
Length ball on off, coming in with the angle there. White looks to flick it but he misses it. The ball raps him on the thigh pad. There is an appeal from the bowler but he soon abandons the appeal.
WIDE! Short of a length outside off, but too wide to make the batsmen play. A wide given by the umpire.

FOUR! They say one brings two and that is what has happened here. Shamim over corrects his line and flights it too full on off. Lellman gets on his front foot and drives it through covers for a boundary. A very good over for the Kiwis, 8 off it.

FOUR! Lellman is off the mark with a boundary. First one off the game and this should give some confidence to the Kiwi batters. It is short and quick outside off, Lellman waits for it and cuts it through backward point for a boundary.
Floated on off, Lellman defends it off the front foot.
Flatter once again and White punches the ball off the back foot towards covers for a single.
Another one that is short and White punches it to covers.
Flatter and outside off, White punches the ball off the back foot towards point.

First runs off the bat of Shoriful. Slightly fuller on off, Ollie defends it wide of point and takes a single to keep the strike. Another solid over from Shoriful. Just one off it. New Zealand struggling to score here.
Play and miss. White falls in the trap and goes to drive this length ball outside off. Luckily for White he does not edge it.
Bouncer! It is down the leg side. White ducks under it and the umpire stretches his arms to signal it as wide.
Good length ball outside off, White does not go chasing after it and leaves it alone.
Length delivery on off, White defends it off the front foot and points the bat to his partner indicating him to wait.
Good length delivery on middle and leg, White tucks it to the leg side.
Full and wide outside off, White looks to drive but misses. Nervy start from the Kiwis here.
Flighted ball around off, Lellman defends it off the front foot towards covers.
Flighted and angled on middle and leg, Lellman looks to tuck it to the leg side but gets it off his thigh pad. The bowler appeals but nothing from the umpire there.
Floated ball around off, Lellman rocks on the back foot and blocks it right under his eyes.
Full and on middle, Lellman drives it towards mid on.
Full and outside off, Lellman drives it to covers.
Tossed up and around off, Lellman leaves it to be.
Shoriful bowls it full and makes it nip in a bit from around off. White offers a solid defensive stroke to get through the over. Another good over from Shoriful. It is a maiden.
Full on off, White pushes it to cover.
Back of a length delivery outside off,  White sees the bounce on it and leaves it alone.
Outside off on a length, White shoulders arms to it.
Fuller on middle and off, White pushes it back to the keeper.
Good length ball outside off, White looks to defend but the ball swings away and squares White all ends up.
Tossed up on off, Lellman pushes it to mid off and gets through the over. Very good over from Shamim. 5 runs but an early wicket of Mariu.
WIDE! Shamim bowls it wide outside off, Lellman leaves it alone and it has been wided.

OUT! CAUGHT! Hossain draws the first blood. New Zealand off to a poor start. The ball just went straight on after pitching up.  Mariu is foxed by it as he pokes it away from his body. The ball just catches the outside edge and goes at a good height towards first slip. Tanzid Hasan there takes the catch.
Full and angled on the pads, White flicks it towards mid-wicket and gets a single.
Full and around off, White prods forward and blocks it off the front foot.
Floated ball on off, White runs it down with an angled bat towards third man and gets a comfortable couple. White off the mark with it.
Tossed  up around off, Mariu drives it towards covers where the fielder misfields and allows a single.
Shamim Hossain to bowl from the other end.

End of a very good first over from Shoriful! He asked questions throughout the 6 balls of his first over. The last ball is another beauty. It is on a length outside off, the previous one came in and this one goes away from the southpaw. White looks to defend but once again cannot get bat on ball. Just a leg bye off the first over of the game.
Another very good ball. Good length ball which comes in off the surface. White looks to defend but misses and gets hit on the thigh pad.
Good ball! Shoriful hits the deck hard just outside off, White has a poke at it but it moves away from the southpaw and beats White all ends up.
New Zealand are off the mark albeit a leg bye. On the pads, Mariu looks to flick but misses. The ball rolls to the leg side off his thigh pad and they take a leg bye.
Shoriful pulls his length back and bowls it on middle and leg, little shape on this one. Mariu defends it towards point and gets bat on ball for the first time today.

Shoriful Islam starts right on the money. He bowls it full outside off, it goes away with the angle. Mariu is tempted to go for the drive and he does but misses it. The two slips in place are just to get that edge from such drives.

Done and dusted with the national anthems and we are all set for the action to begin. Bangladesh players are in a huddle before they take their respective positions in the field. Rhys Mariu and Ollie White will open the batting for New Zealand. Shoriful Islam will start the proceedings for Bangladesh. Three slips in place for him.
The players are out for their National Anthems. It will be Bangladesh's first followed by New Zealand's. We are not far away from the action to begin.

New Zealand U19 (Playing XI) - Rhys Mariu, Ollie White, Fergus Lellman, Jesse Tashkoff (C), Beckham Wheeler-Greenall, Quinn Sunde (WK), Nicholas Lidstone (In for Simon Keene), Adithya Ashok, David Hancock, Kristian Clarke, Joey Field.

Bangladesh (Unchanged Playing XI) - Parvez Hossain Emon, Tanzid Hasan, Mahmudul Hasan Joy, Towhid Hridoy, Shahadat Hossain, Akbar Ali (C/WK), Shamim Hossain, Hasan Murad, Tanzim Hasan Sakib, Rakibul Hasan, Shoriful Islam.

New Zealand skipper, Jesse Tashkoff says they would have done the same as the conditions will help to bowl later on but now he is looking to add runs. Tells they look to keep things close and keep the run rate in check in the middle overs. Tells it would have been better to have played a game in the break but adds they have trained in the break days. Informs Nicholas Lidstone comes in for Simon Keene.

Bangladesh skipper, Akbar Ali says that they are bowling first as it rained last night and there is some moisture. Adds he hopes to restrict them to a low total. Informs they are unchanged. Says they are confident  but they will need to play good cricket to beat them.
Toss - It's time for the flip of the coin. Up goes the coin and it lands in the favour of Bangladesh. Bangladesh opt to bowl first.

Pitch Report -  Dominic Cork and JP Duminy are down for the pitch report. Cork says there is a bit of moisture and humidity in the air and that will help the bowlers to swing the ball. Duminy says that both teams will feel the toss is important not just because of the weather but also because of the live grass on it and there will be some bounce on offer because of it.

India are in the final, who will join them? Will it be the young Bangla Tigers or will it be the young Kiwis? Hello and welcome to the second semi-final of the ICC Under-19 World Cup 2020 between New Zealand and Bangladesh. New Zealand overcame the Carribean threat to book a spot in the Semi-Finals. Whereas, Bangladesh romped home against hosts, South Africa by a huge margin. Both teams will look to outplay each other and come out on the winning side. The Asian underdogs are starting favourites as they boast of a good bowling attack especially spin. Who will book a place in finals? Stay tuned as Toss and team updates are not far away.
